title: Hybrid attention kernel adapter + prefill/decode scheduling strategy
creator: Lina Duarte
description: Goal: Ship a stable hybrid adapter that can route requests between FlashAttention v2 and v3-compatible kernels while preserving latency SLAs and eliminating recent regressions observed during large prefill workloads. This ticket covers design and implementation of a lightweight adapter layer (no binary dependency changes), a prefill-aware scheduler shim that coordinates kernel choice + microtiling, a memory estimator for KV cache sizing during prefill, expanded telemetry for kernel selection decisions, and a guarded rollout plan with automated rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Hybrid adapter routes >=95% of production request patterns to the optimal kernel variant without increasing median decode latency by >5%
No OOM regressions observed on prefill-heavy benchmarks (1M tokens simulated) during 24h soak
Telemetry emits kernel_choice, reason_code, memory_estimate, and schedule_decision events for every prefills/decodes in canary traffic
Canary rollout with 2% traffic shows equivalent or improved p95 latency and cost/unit compared to baseline; automatic rollback trigger implemented
Design doc and unit/integration tests merged; release notes and rollback playbook published
design_notes: We will implement an adapter shim that exposes a common kernel selection API: score_candidates(request_features) -> ordered list. Request_features include seq_len, batch_size, kv_present, quantization_profile, layout_hint. The adapter keeps a tiny local registry of kernel capability tuples (e.g., supports_prefill, max_chunk, workspace_ratio). A memory estimator predicts KV cache working set for prefill and decode phases to avoid surprising OOMs. For layout differences between FA v2 and v3, implement fast on-the-fly transpose path only for small warmup batches; large batches must pick the compatible kernel. Prefill scheduler: schedule_prefill_batches prioritizes low-latency models for short-prefill requests and batching-friendly kernels for bulk-prefill; we add a microtiling step to split oversized prefill into decode-friendly chunks while preserving KV ordering. Performance heuristics initially seeded from offline benchmarks; later updated by a lightweight online learner (phase 2).
implementation_steps: Prototype kernel capability registry and scoring API (ENG-130001.1)
Add memory estimator for KV cache and integrate into selection path (ENG-130001.2)
Implement prefill scheduler shim with microtiling and layout-aware fallback (ENG-130001.3)
E2E test harness for prefill-heavy workloads (local and CI) (ENG-130001.5)
Canary rollout orchestration and automated rollback criteria (ENG-130001.6)
Post-rollout regression checklist and cost analysis (ENG-130001.7)
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring API and memory estimator edge cases
Integration tests: single-request prefill->decode transition for mixed-model traffic
Benchmark suite: 10K synthetic prefill scenarios across seq_len distribution (8..8192) comparing v2, v3, hybrid
Soak test: 24h prefill-heavy workload on canary pool with telemetry validation
Safety tests: intentional workspace_budget shrink to validate graceful fallback and no crash behavior
rollback_plan: Immediate traffic divert to runtime-1.21 kernel-config (baseline) via routing flag
Revert adapter flag in console and disable hybrid selection in canary group
Run incident runbook: collect kernel_choice telemetry, memory_estimate traces, and top-20 failing request fingerprints
Hotfix: pin problematic model variants to known-good kernel until root cause fixed
metrics_and_dashboards: p50/p95 decode latency per-kernel and aggregate
OOM count and workspace pressure by kernel
prefill->decode transition latencies and KV cache growth curves
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: layout conversion path adds CPU overhead -> Mitigation: restrict conversion to <5% of requests and measure cost impact
Risk: memory estimator underestimates rare long-context requests -> Mitigation: conservative safety margin + runtime quota enforcement
Risk: online learner might overfit to short-term noise -> Mitigation: decay window and manual QA for heuristic updates
Risk: regression slip on mixed-quant runs -> Mitigation: explicit compatibility matrix and canary flush for quantized model families
